passage:
The school newspaper printed the wrong date for the music concert. It said Friday instead of Thursday.
When the mistake was found, the newspaper team felt terrible. They quickly put notices on classroom doors and sent messages to teachers.
Most students still came on the correct day, but the team apologized in the next issue.
Their teacher said, "Mistakes happen. What matters is how clearly and quickly you correct them."
After that, the team made a checking list. One person checked names, another checked dates, and another checked places.
The newspaper became better because of the mistake. It taught the team that responsibility does not mean never being wrong. It means taking the correction seriously.
